articles.description:
Today I improved my Go Conference Booking App by learning how Go handles collections and loops. I explored arrays, slices, infinite loops, range, strings.Fields(), and the blank identifier.
Here’s what I learned:
An array in Go has a fixed size.
Example:
var numbers [3]int = [3]int{10, 20, 30}

Fixed length 
If I used an array for bookings, it would look like this:
var bookings [50]string

But this is limiting because:
The size is fixed
Harder to manage dynamic data
That’s why slices are usually preferred.
Instead of using a fixed array, I used a slice to store bookings:
bookings := []string{}

Every time a user books:
bookings = append(bookings, fName+" "+lName)

What I Learned:
Slices don’t have a fixed size
append() adds new elements
Slices are the most common way to manage lists in Go
…

articles.author: Michael Bello
articles.description:
The problem


Every developer has been here: you're staring at 0 */4 * * 1-5 in a config file 
I got tired of that. So I built Cron.Explain, a free tool that decodes any cron expression into plain English instantly.
🔗 https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app
Paste any cron expression and you get three things:
1. Plain English explanation
0 9 * * 1-5 → "At 9:00 AM, on Monday through Friday"
2. Field-by-field breakdown
3. Next 5 run times
It also ships a free REST API — no key required:
curl -X POST https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app/api/explain \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cron": "0 9 * * 1-5"}'

Response:
{
  "expression": "0 9 * * 1-5",
  "explanation": "At 9:00 AM, on Monday through Friday",
  "fields": { ... },
  "nextRuns": ["2026-02-23T09:00:00.000Z", ...]
}

The interesting part: I didn't use any external cron parsing libraries. 
The core is a matchesField(value, n, min) function that handles all the special cron characters: *, */n, n-m, n,m, and n/m.
The next-run calculator works by starting from the current minute and incrementing forward, checking each minute against all 5 fields until it finds 5 matches. It caps at 500,000 iterations to handle edge cases like rare monthly schedules.
React + Vite (frontend)
Netlify Functions (serverless API)
Zero dependencies for the parser
IBM Plex Mono font because it felt right for a dev tool
I'm thinking about adding:
Cron job monitoring (ping a URL, alert if it hasn't run)
Reverse builder (describe a schedule in English, get the cron)
More languages in the API docs
The code is open source on GitHub. Would love feedback, especially on cron expressions that break the parser — there are definitely edge cases I haven't covered.
🔗 Live tool: https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app
API docs: https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app/docs
articles.title: I built a free cron expression decoder, here's how it works under the hood
